newsitem.title: USA: Cohen presents military plan to lawmakers.
newsitem.headline: Cohen presents military plan to lawmakers.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Cohen on Thursday presented his new proposal for U.S. military strategy and force cuts to key members of Congress and committee staff directors.
Cohen made no comment at a photo opportunity at a breakfast meeting attened by about 30 Pentagon officials and senior lawmakers and staffers from four committees of the House and Senate.

Pentagon officials have said that the quadrennial defence review (QDR) plan, due to be formally made public on Monday, calls for base closings and shrinking the size of jet fighter programmes, but would cut only some 60,000 troops from the 1.4 million member military. It is designed to set strategy, force levels and arms modernisation into the 21st century.

Cohen, who retired earlier this year as a Republican senator from Maine, was flanked at his table by Chairmen Floyd Spense, a South Carolina Republican, of the House National Security Committee and Chairman Ted Stevens, an Alaska Republican, of the Senate Appropriations Committee.
Senior Republicans and Democrats from the Senate Armed Services Committee and House Appropriations Committees also attended.
Pentagon officials said Cohen would outline the plan for former Defence Secretaries William Perry, Harold Brown, Dick Cheney, Elliot Richardson and Donald Rumsfeld at a private Pentagon lunch.
